elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: "shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, excluding its principles of conflict of laws." Wisconsin replaced with New York; conflicts carve-out retained.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.2: "the parties consent to venue in the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, New York for the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere." Both court tiers, the county anchor, exclusivity over the merits, and the narrow temporary-injunctive carve-out are all present in operative text.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1 selects New York law; no Delaware, California, or England and Wales choice appears (the fallback is only offered in the margin comment, which is not operative).

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.2 fixes New York County courts, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: 22.1 supplies New York governing law and 22.2 supplies exclusive state-and-federal New York County merits jurisdiction with only a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out, which the checklist element expressly contemplates and which does not create a broader alternate merits forum.

Fallback level is incomplete (both fallback elements not met), but that is immaterial because one full level is satisfied; the alternative Delaware/California/England-and-Wales positions are correctly reserved in the comment rather than drafted into the text.

Minimality holds: only the jurisdiction words and the forum designation changed. The article/adjective fix from "an exclusive jurisdiction" to "the exclusive jurisdiction" is grammatical necessity flowing from the forum substitution, not a substantive deletion, and the "for the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere" language is required by the selected preferred element. No survival tails, fee-shifting, procedures, or other model-language extras were added.

Intent preserved: the second sentence of 22.2 — the parties' consent to jurisdiction where a judgment debtor's assets are located, including judgments rendered "through arbitration or litigation" — is retained verbatim, so the judgment-enforcement mechanic and its cross-references survive without contradiction. The retained reference to arbitration is an enforcement mechanic only (Article 15 is escalation, not an arbitration agreement), so it does not conflict with the new exclusive court forum or create a foreign-seated arbitration overlay.
No dangling cross-references or undefined terms are introduced; "New York County, New York" is self-defining and the conflict-of-laws exclusion continues to attach to the newly chosen law.
